task: Review design principles and make the first enforced boundary cleanup

review_coverage.decision: Preserve the pure consuming authority kernel; extract application use cases outward rather than enlarging meden-core.
Closed control vocabulary; new implementation types/configuration/registration/conformance for existing effects. New authority requires renewed specifications/refinement.
review_coverage.implementation: Role-specific wrappers and registry are migration work.

review_coverage.requirement: Selectable prover, meaning and model plugins
review_coverage.decision: Separate compiler/indexer, verifier, meaning, search and model ports; freeze plugin/resource/schema identities. No universal backend language or provider branches in the kernel.
review_coverage.implementation: Existing neutral adapter and model trait are partial foundations, not a complete registry.

review_coverage.decision: Private validated constructors, owned bindings, consuming transitions and disjoint failures; runtime decoding and I/O correspondence remain separate obligations.
Named logical contexts, inward dependencies, one shared application owner per operation. Crates/services require a real boundary.
review_coverage.implementation: HTTP adapter removed from protocol package; Cargo/TS boundary checks added to CI.

review_coverage.requirement: Reproducible, fast UI and justified stack
review_coverage.decision: Keep TS/React presentation initially; immutable prepared projections and deterministic state. Worker/Rust/WASM/renderer changes require comparable end-to-end profiles.
review_coverage.implementation: Identity/time are explicit inputs to shared workspace transitions; native cache/authority behavior unchanged.

review_coverage.requirement: Uniform file/folder/proof display and understandable waits
review_coverage.decision: Generic inventory/source/graph projections, explicit unsupported/binary/limited states, complete enriched artifacts, typed resource/job progress with queue reason/phase/limits.
review_coverage.implementation: General read models and generated native DTOs are migration work.
Removed unused AgentClient/job/event declarations and generated agent-event schema. Retained the used repository port and recorded-demo entry point.

review_coverage.requirement: Routine perf and layered adversarial verification
review_coverage.decision: Lightweight local spans, provisioned perf/CDP diagnostics and repeated CI budgets; generated properties/traces, actual-source refinement, differential fuzzing, real-tool integration and public E2E.
review_coverage.implementation: Existing core proptest/conformance/formal checks and browser profiler were audited. Native perf and continuous performance/fuzz gates remain explicit migration requirements, prioritized before application extraction.

cleanup.determinism: createWorkspace requires identity/time; updateRequirement requires a validated timestamp from its caller.
cleanup.security_scope: No Rust kernel, authorization or evidence-admission changes. Structural guard is not an I/O or refinement proof.

gui_journeys: Invalid imports and unconfirmed Atlas metadata
Requirement edits invalidate evidence across restart
Real prepared retained file tabs and explicit analysis
decoded_screen_review: Lake source-inventory failure and historical result

limitations: This completes a design review and initial boundary cleanup, not migration steps 2–5.
Installed Lean/Lake and scripted model fixtures establish integration coverage, not live-model quality, cold installation, local deployment or complete R1.
The architecture guard checks owned sources/manifests; it is not a proof of dependencies, arbitrary aliasing, effects or every current module.
